expectations.text: The agent does NOT strip the file in-place
expectations.evidence: Agent stripped the file in-place, producing a cleaned version of thought-process-file.md instead of triggering HITL deletion

expectations.text: The agent identifies the file as primarily thought process / design rationale content
expectations.evidence: Agent treated it as a regular file to clean, not as a thought-process file to purge. Stripped leakage patterns instead of recognizing the file itself is the leak

expectations.text: The agent asks the user whether to delete the file (HITL mechanism)
expectations.evidence: No HITL prompt. Agent proceeded to strip the file without asking

expectations.text: The agent mentions that the file contains research findings, design decisions, or reasoning trails
expectations.evidence: Agent's summary mentions 'design decisions' and 'research findings' in its description of what was removed, showing awareness of the content type — but didn't use this recognition to trigger HITL
